definition: The neural network converting acoustic representations (mel spectrograms) into waveforms.
details: The neural network converting acoustic representations (mel spectrograms) into waveforms. HiFi-GAN-class GAN vocoders dominate production for speed and quality; the vocoder ceiling determines how natural any two-stage TTS can sound.

explainer.lead: A vocoder in modern speech systems is the neural network converting acoustic representations, typically mel spectrograms, into waveforms. It matters because in two-stage TTS the vocoder sets the ceiling on how natural the output can sound.

tiers.eli5: It's the final step that turns a rough sketch of sound into actual audio you can hear.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers place it after the acoustic model in two-stage TTS and favor HiFi-GAN-class GAN vocoders for speed and quality; a pitfall is that no acoustic model can sound better than the vocoder allows.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it maps a mel spectrogram to a waveform; HiFi-GAN-class GAN vocoders dominate production, and the vocoder ceiling bounds two-stage TTS naturalness.

explainer.example: An acoustic model outputs a mel spectrogram of a sentence, and the vocoder renders it into an audible waveform.
